fn has(xs: List[Int], x: Int) -> Bool
  requires len(xs) >= 0
  ensures result == contains(xs, x)
  effects pure
  example has([1, 4, 6], 4) == true
  example has([1, 4, 6], 5) == false
  example has([], 1) == false
{
  match xs {
    [] => false
    [h, ..t] => h == x or has(t, x)
  }
}

fn at_pos(xs: List[Int], x: Int, i: Int) -> Bool
  requires len(xs) >= 0
  ensures result == (i >= 0 and i < len(xs) and xs[i] == x)
  effects pure
  example at_pos([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, 2) == true
  example at_pos([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, 1) == false
  example at_pos([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, 7) == false
  example at_pos([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, -1) == false
{
  if i < 0 then false else match xs {
    [] => false
    [h, ..t] => if i == 0 then h == x else at_pos(t, x, i - 1)
  }
}

fn search_ok(xs: List[Int], x: Int, r: Option[Int]) -> Bool
  requires len(xs) >= 0
  ensures result == (match r { None => not contains(xs, x)
    Some(i) => i >= 0 and i < len(xs) and xs[i] == x })
  effects pure
  example search_ok([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, Some(2)) == true
  example search_ok([1, 4, 6, 9], 5, None) == true
  example search_ok([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, None) == false
  example search_ok([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, Some(1)) == false
  example search_ok([1, 4, 6, 9], 5, Some(1)) == false
{
  match r {
    None => not has(xs, x)
    Some(i) => at_pos(xs, x, i)
  }
}

  example binary_search([], 3) == None
  example binary_search([1, 4, 6, 9], 1) == Some(0)

  requires len(xs) >= 0
  ensures forall x in result: x % 2 == 0
  ensures forall x in xs: (x % 2 == 0 and count(result, x) == count(xs, x)) or (x % 2 != 0 and count(result, x) == 0)
  effects pure
  example evens_of([1, 2, 3, 4]) == [2, 4]
  example evens_of([]) == []
  example evens_of([5, 7]) == []
{

    [] => []

  }
}
